t: #2341 Maximum Number of Pairs in Array
o: Repeatedly remove pairs of equal numbers; report how many pairs form and how many leftovers remain. Since pairing within equal values is independent across values, each value with frequency c contributes floor(c/2) pairs and c mod 2 leftovers. Example [1,3,2,1,3,2,2] has counts 1:2, 2:3, 3:2 -> 3 pairs, 1 leftover.
k: Pairing is independent per distinct value.
Values are bounded by 100, so a counting array works as well as a hash map.

a.i: Count occurrences of each value, then aggregate floor(c/2) and c%2. One pass to count, one pass over at most 101 distinct values.
s: Count frequencies with a hash map or 101-slot array.
Accumulate pairs += freq // 2 and leftover += freq % 2.
a.t: O(n + V) where V = 101 distinct values.

w: Trivial problem; the only care point is reading the required output format [pairs, leftovers]. Follow-up: return the actual pairs, or handle a generalized 'remove groups of size k'.
